idFamilies.JAVA-XNA: A gap between CNA-Java and the original XNA 4.0 contract.
idFamilies.JAVA-NATIVE: A gap at the CNA C ABI boundary: a route, a shape or a verification.
idFamilies.JAVA-EXT: A CNA capability outside XNA 4.0, belonging under org.openeggbert.cna.extensions.
idFamilies.JAVA-TEMPLATE: Work in the sibling cna-java-template consumer canary.
idFamilies.JAVA-UPSTREAM: Blocked on cnanext or sharp-runtimenext. Never worked around in Java.

tasks.title: Keep XNA's Dispose() name and add close() as the Java bridge
tasks.authority: 36 CLR types declaring a public parameterless Dispose

tasks.compatibility: Additive. 33 types gained Dispose(); no member was removed and every close() call site still compiles.

tasks.title: Project the GamerServices and Avatar families

tasks.title: Project Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net
tasks.currentState: The whole namespace was missing; 23 types.
tasks.expectedState: Sessions, discovery, rosters, machines, packets and the nine session events projected, session and gamer state backed by CNA.

tasks.title: Raise the nine NetworkSession events and the two SignedInGamer events from CNA
tasks.currentState: The event members existed and accepted listeners; no native producer raised them.
tasks.expectedState: Hand-written JNI records each event and Java drains the record right after pumping the dispatcher or the session, so every event arrives on the game thread during Update, as XNA raises it.
tasks.blocker: None. It needs the callback lifetime work that the media and storage families already have, applied to eleven more callbacks.

tasks.title: Inventory the Content Pipeline build-time profile
tasks.authority: the seven Content Pipeline assemblies, SHA-256 pinned in xna40-content-pipeline.json
tasks.currentState: Measured. 128 reference types and 743 members; 125 of the types are absent and 3 are already present from the runtime projection. By namespace: Graphics 47, the framework 32, Processors 28, Intermediate 7, Compiler 5, Audio 5, MSBuild Tasks 4.
tasks.expectedState: A decision, recorded with its evidence in docs/content-pipeline-decision.md: partial/interop. CNA-Java consumes compiled content and does not reimplement Microsoft's build-time pipeline. Four measured reasons, none of them size: two namespaces need MSBuild and System.Xml types the pinned corpus does not contain; the ten importers wrap Windows-only native technology whose bytes cannot be reproduced; every ContentTypeWriter's one abstract member returns a CLR assembly-qualified reader name, so emitting .xnb from Java would produce files no XNA runtime reads; and CNA already ships its own compiler and format, which the binding now consumes through org.openeggbert.cna.extensions.content.
tasks.note: The profile stays pinned and is deliberately not measured against the runtime target: a build-time contract is not a runtime regression gate.

tasks.title: Expose CNA's extended graphics layer
tasks.currentState: 1,733 routes classified CNA_EXTENSION_CANDIDATE; none reachable from Java.
tasks.expectedState: org.openeggbert.cna.extensions.graphics projects the seven identities, the render pipeline settings, the physically based material and the ASCII, CRT and depth post-process effects. Availability is truthful and NOT_SUPPORTED keeps its own identity.

tasks.title: Expose CNA's runtime and device extensions
tasks.authority: core_ext.h, devices.h, sensors.h, input_haptics.h, input_joystick.h, input_text.h, input_cursor.h, input_devices.h
tasks.currentState: Six families are projected: the runtime's own identity and logger, the host devices, typed text plus the mouse cursor, the four host motion sensors, device and sensor enumeration with hot plug, and raw joysticks, haptics and the modern game-pad, keyboard, mouse and touch capabilities.
tasks.expectedState: Typed Java facades under the extension namespace, never inside Microsoft.Xna.Framework. Availability is CNA's answer everywhere: an absent sensor reports NotSupported and refuses a reading rather than answering zeros, a closed haptic device is a safe no-op, and an unconnected joystick captures empty.

tasks.title: Expose the .cnb content format
tasks.currentState: 108 of the 272 routes are bound and reached: the container layer, the document, the checked byte reader, the texture data, the writer and the Texture2D encoder and decoder. A game can read a .cnb file, walk its chunks, verify their checksums, decode a texture and upload it as an XNA Texture2D, and a Java build step can write a .cnb file of its own schema. The remaining 164 are the model, sprite-font, sound, song, video, curve, animation-clip and .cnj families, plus the loader registry.
tasks.expectedState: The remaining asset families projected as they earn a consumer. The loader registry is the one part that needs a design decision rather than more binding: cna_cnb_loader_invoke hands back a void* the callback produced, which has no Java meaning, so a Java loader registry has to be a Java-side dispatch over the document rather than a projection of CNA's.
tasks.note: Every fixture is produced by CNA's own encoder and writer and read back by CNA's own parser, so a successful read means the file is a real one rather than that two hand-written halves share a misunderstanding.

tasks.title: Use the whole-buffer vertex upload route
tasks.currentState: The route is loaded, so the library must export it, but no JNI entry point reaches it: SetData always takes the windowed form.
tasks.expectedState: An upload that starts at the beginning takes CNA's whole-buffer route; a windowed one takes the windowed route. Both are now reached, and boundButUnreached is empty.

tasks.title: Bind the native Model routes behind the managed XNB model graph
tasks.currentState: 127 routes deferred; Load<Model> was managed-only, and the audit asked what native backing would add.
tasks.expectedState: The XNA Model graph reaches CNA. CnaModel.From(Model) builds CNA's own model over the buffers and effects the XNA model already owns -- retained, not copied, so nothing is uploaded twice -- and CNA then draws it in one call and computes its bone transforms. models.h is fully classified: 184 extension candidates, 31 not useful in Java, and one deferred route, the loader JAVA-UPSTREAM-004 blocks.
tasks.note: Load<Model> deliberately stays on the managed XNB reader. XNB records the effect's type and the reader builds the BasicEffect an XNA game casts to; CNA publishes a loaded effect as a handle whose type is only a name, so routing the strict load through CNA would break (BasicEffect) part.getEffect(). The measurement is in CnaModelTests, which reads one authored .xnb through both runtimes and compares their graphs bone for bone.

tasks.title: Bind the remaining input routes
tasks.currentState: 132 routes were deferred. The audit found that none of them was an XNA-shaped route lacking backing: the whole XNA input surface -- game-pad state, capabilities and vibration, keyboard state, mouse state and position, touch state, capabilities, panel and gestures -- was already bound.
tasks.expectedState: Every input route classified with a stated reason and no deferred remainder. 39 became bound CNA extensions (modern game-pad identity, battery, light bar, trigger motors, touchpad, button labels and sensors; keyboard scancode and layout naming; mouse capture, relative mode, desktop position and the click event; mouse-driven touch emulation). The remaining 92 are NOT_USEFUL_IN_JAVA: construction, equality, hashing, string form and indexing of XNA's input value types, which are managed structs in XNA and managed values here, plus two CNA test seams.

tasks.title: Add a truthful modern-CNA canary to the template

tasks.title: Native StorageContainer path containment
tasks.currentState: Fixed upstream and revalidated against the live 0.21.0 library, not against a commit message. Asked directly in C, past the Java guard: cna_storage_container_file_exists refuses '../escaped.sav', 'a/../../escaped.sav' and '/absolute.sav' with CNA_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT, and accepts an ordinary name, so the refusal is containment rather than a route that stopped working.
tasks.expectedState: The guarantee is the runtime's. Java keeps its own guard as well -- it produces XNA's exception and message deterministically whatever backend is loaded -- but it is no longer the only thing standing there, and a test now asserts CNA's refusal past the guard so that stays true.
tasks.blocker: cnanext storage: cna_storage_container_* accept a path containing parent traversal.

The nine that fail are CApiCoverageMatrix, CApiLimitations, CApiReleaseGate, CApi_CoreExtSmoke, CApi_ContentSmoke, CApi_DevicesSmoke, CApi_MediaPlayerSmoke, CApi_AudioSmoke and CApi_AudioUnavailableSmoke. tasks.title: Project CNA's text composition and candidate events
tasks.currentState: Typed characters were projected; composition text and candidate lists were not, because each carries a string the fixed five-long event record cannot hold.
tasks.expectedState: A second transport that owns heap copies made inside CNA's callback, hands them to Java as byte arrays in one call that frees the record before it returns, and is merged with the numeric queue by a sequence stamped when CNA raised the event, so one order comes out of two queues. TextComposition and TextCandidates sit on top of it in the input extension package.
tasks.blocker: None upstream. It needs a second event transport, not a CNA change.

tasks.title: Reach or unbind the 162 routes no Java call site touches
tasks.currentState: 162 bound routes had a generated JNI entry point that no Java source called. All of them are resolved: seven were reached and 155 unbound with a rule saying why. boundWithoutJavaCallSite is 0 and nativeCoverageCheck now fails on it, so it cannot regrow. Bound routes went 1,570 to 1,418 and XNA_BACKING 976 to 985.
tasks.expectedState: Every bound route reaches a Java call site, or is unbound with a stated reason. The reasons are families rather than one-offs: PacketReader and PacketWriter stay managed BinaryReader and BinaryWriter so Position and Length keep XNA's meaning over one cursor; a Begin/End pair is projected over CNA's synchronous route because its asynchronous form completes before its own begin returns; value construction and equality are Java's as they are for the vector families; a read-only collection's mutators can have no call site because the Java member throws as XNA's does; a factory for an object the projection receives has nothing to make; and CNA's application-rendered Guide, its avatar rendering and a discovered session's address are extensions XNA has no member for.
tasks.blocker: None. It is measurement plus per-family judgement, not an upstream change.
tasks.note: Three reaches were real gaps rather than tidying: a failed join now raises XNA's NetworkSessionJoinException carrying the error CNA recorded instead of a generic failure with a Java default, and a whole-array send or receive takes CNA's whole-buffer route as VertexBuffer.SetData already did. A fourth was refused by the full-profile gate: asking CNA for a gamer collection's membership would have declared contains and indexOf on GamerCollection, which CLR's does not declare.

tasks.title: cna_content_manager_load_model produces a model that segfaults during teardown
tasks.currentState: Loading any .xnb whose meshes have parts through CNA's own content manager gives a model that crashes when it is released. Reproduced in C with no Java involved: cna_game_create, cna_game_get_graphics_device, cna_content_manager_create, cna_content_manager_load_model("cube") over cnanext's own tests/assets/xnb/monogame/windows/uncompressed/BlenderDefaultCube.xnb, then cna_model_destroy. SIGSEGV in Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics::ModelMeshPart::setTagProperty called from (anonymous namespace)::PartResource::~PartResource. The crash does not need the model to be walked first, and it also happens when the caller never destroys the model and lets the content manager and game tear it down, so there is no calling order that avoids it. A model assembled by hand with cna_model_create_with_parents over a mesh with a part destroys cleanly, so the fault is on the content-load path rather than in the model family.
tasks.expectedState: A content-loaded model releases without faulting, so a binding can offer CNA's own loader.
tasks.blocker: cnanext content: PartResource's destructor reaches a ModelMeshPart whose owner is already gone. cnanext's own CApi_ContentSmoke fixtures are models with one bone and no meshes, which is why the path is uncovered upstream.

tasks.title: Three value types leaked the CNA handles they owned
tasks.currentState: Fixed, and it was three types rather than one. NetworkSessionProperties' public constructor, all four AvatarDescription paths, and every LeaderboardEntry created an owned CNA handle that nothing released; none of the three is IDisposable in XNA, so a game had nothing to close and no way to know. LeaderboardReader.getEntries was the worst: every entry CNA hands out is an owned copy, so the leak grew with each call of an ordinary getter. Measured: cna_network_session_properties_destroy answers CNA_RESULT_THREAD from any thread but the creating one, so a Cleaner could not release any of them either.
tasks.expectedState: org.openeggbert.cna.internal.NativeDeferredRelease records the handle when the Java object becomes unreachable and the owning thread releases it at the next FrameworkDispatcher.Update, which is where this binding already does deferred native work. A session-owned list registers nothing, because the session frees it.

tasks.title: Two gates could not see an ABI migration go wrong
tasks.currentState: Fixed. NativeBindings.COMPILED_ABI_VERSION is what a game hits at load time and was hand-maintained: the 0.21.0 migration moved the manifest and the probe and left it at 0.20, which every gate passed and which then refused the library. And the test task treated neither native library as an input, so rebuilding libcna_c_api left the suite up to date and reporting the previous run's results against a different library.
tasks.expectedState: nativeAbiCheck fails on JAVA_COMPILED_ABI_DRIFT, with a negative-mutation test; the test task declares both native libraries as inputs.

tasks.title: Project the gamer-services capabilities XNA has no member for
tasks.currentState: The Guide slice is done: org.openeggbert.cna.extensions.gamerservices projects the pending on-screen keyboard and message box, CNA's own renderer for them, the outcomes a game reports back, and the achievements pane. 16 routes reached. The avatar slice (10 routes) and a discovered session's host and port (4) are still classified extension candidates.
tasks.expectedState: Three coherent slices under org.openeggbert.cna.extensions. CNA's Guide hands the application the pending on-screen keyboard or message box and asks it to draw, where XNA's Guide draws itself: 14 routes, and the useful shape is a typed pending-request record plus a render call, not a projection of the raw routes. CNA's avatar layer exposes real rendering and the clip and content names behind the canonical presets: 10 routes. And a discovered session carries the host and port it was found at, which AvailableNetworkSession does not name: 4 routes.
tasks.blocker: None. It needs an API design per slice, not a CNA change.
